title: Reject impossible calibrator certificate dates
prompt:
Fix calendar validation only in lib/ohworks-calibrator-traceability.ts. Evidence: the timestamp helper at lines 158-160 accepts any Z-suffixed string that Date.parse normalizes; certificate validation at lines 291-295 then treats that normalized instant as real. I reproduced a single declared reference lot with certificateExpiresAt='2026-02-30T08:00:00.000Z', assignedValue=100, assignedValueUncertainty=0.5 and runAt='2026-02-20T08:00:00.000Z' returning decision='traceable'. February 30 must not establish a current certificate. The user-facing instrument readiness view imports this evaluator at lib/ohworks-demo-instrument-readiness-view.ts:3.

Make the local timestamp validator verify actual calendar components, preserving valid UTC timestamps with and without fractional seconds. Invalid certificate dates must return the existing certificate-timestamp-invalid reason and not_traceable decision; invalid run dates must retain run-timestamp-invalid. Keep chain traversal and expiry boundary behavior unchanged. Do not introduce a shared production helper that overlaps another job.

Add tests/ohworks/calibrator-calendar-validity.test.ts for February 30, non-leap February 29, April 31, valid leap day, and invalid run dates. Run node --import tsx --test tests/ohworks/calibrator-calendar-validity.test.ts tests/ohworks/calibrator-traceability.test.ts tests/ohworks/demo-instrument-readiness-view.test.ts. The existing evaluator suite passed during planning and the defect was reproduced with assertions. Only synthetic data is in scope. Avoid credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflows, package.json and auth. Keep this one production-file change; work on the assigned branch you are on.
